overview.remote.cleanup.text:
Find port candidates worth cleaning up on this server. This connection is read-only, so only suggest; I'll do the actual cleanup from the dashboard or Claude Code on the server.

1. Use list_ports and who_uses_what to see each port's owner (control) and the devices using it now.
2. Candidates: dev servers nobody is using now · several ports with the same name or project · apps whose http is null or 5xx.
3. Leave out: portboard itself, pinned ports, system ports.

Results as a table: port · name · control · reason · suggestion (stop / unexpose from tailnet / leave as is).
Last-use history isn't visible over this connection, so say so for candidates you're unsure about.
overview.remote.status.text:
Give me a short summary of the Portboard server ({host}) status.

What to read: if you can read the resource `portboard://status`, that alone is enough; otherwise use the list_devices, list_ports and who_uses_what tools.

Format:
1. One conclusion on the first line: "All good" or "Needs a look: …".
2. Devices: online n / total n. Only call out the ones that shouldn't be off (compute-pool hosts, this server). Skip phones that are off.
3. compute-pool: hosts whose state is not ok · agent-busy · agent-away, with their state.
4. In use: one line per service, saying who is using it.
5. 🔔 down: port, name, since when (only in the status resource).
6. New devices: how many are not acknowledged yet. Leave out if none.

This connection is read-only and can't change anything. If something is wrong, only suggest what to check.

prompts.cleanup.desc: Finds unused dev servers and duplicate ports and suggests cleanup candidates in a table (doesn't run anything)
prompts.cleanup.text:
Find ports on this server worth cleaning up and suggest them. Don't stop or change anything; only suggest.

1. Use list_ports(include_system: false) and who_uses to see each port's owner (control), group, lastUsed and the devices using it now.
2. Candidates: nobody is using it now and lastUsed is older than {days} days or missing · several dev servers for the same project · apps whose http is null or 5xx · only a tailscale serve (servedUrl) left that nobody opens.
3. Leave out: portboard itself, system ports, pinned ports, alert=true (🔔) ports. Ports in the same group go on one line.

Results as a table: port · name · control · last used · reason · suggestion (stop_service / unexpose_port / leave as is).
When unsure, look at the usage history with service_detail(port).
Once I pick numbers, run them one at a time; for a plain process (control is process: pid …), first tell me where it was started from.

prompts.newDev.lead: I want to start a new dev server.
prompts.newDev.leadProject: I want to start a new dev server: {project}.
prompts.newDev.text:
1. Get a free port with free_port({args}). Don't guess a port.
2. Start the server on that port with the framework's flag (Vite `--port N`, Next.js `-p N`, Django `runserver 127.0.0.1:N`, otherwise `PORT=N`), binding to 127.0.0.1 by default.
   If it should keep running, start it detached from the terminal (e.g. systemd --user or nohup) and tell me how you started it.
3. Check with list_ports(query: "N") that it is listening and answers HTTP (status). If it doesn't come up, read tail_logs(port: N).
4. Opening it from other devices (Mac, iPhone):
   - If scope is loopback and canExpose=true: expose_port(N) → servedUrl (https://<host>.ts.net:N, opens only on tailnet devices).
   - If the result has an enableUrl, Serve isn't turned on for the tailnet yet: pass that link on to me.
   - If it already binds to tailnet/all, use directUrl without exposing.
   - Don't use Funnel (public internet).
5. Finish with a summary: port, how it was started, the URL to open, how to stop it.
prompts.newDev.title: Start a new dev server
prompts.status.desc: Devices, compute-pool, services in use, 🔔 ports that are down and new devices in one summary
prompts.status.text:
Give me a short summary of the Portboard server status.

What to read (if you can read resources, `portboard://status` alone is enough; otherwise use the tools):
- list_devices: which devices are online, compute-pool host state
- list_ports: listening ports, and ports with alert=true but listening=false (🔔 down)
- who_uses: who is using which service right now
- list_new_devices: new devices not acknowledged yet

Format:
1. One conclusion on the first line: "All good" or "Needs a look: …".
2. Devices: online n / total n. Only call out the ones that shouldn't be off (compute-pool hosts, this server). Skip phones that are off.
3. compute-pool: hosts whose state is not ok · agent-busy · agent-away, with their state.
4. In use: one line per service, saying who is using it.
5. 🔔 down: port, name, since when.
6. New devices: name, first service used. Leave out if none.

If something is wrong, only suggest the next steps one by one; don't run actions like restart_service · stop_service · expose_port until I say so.

prompts.why.end: Finish with the cause in one line + how to fix it. Ask before running restart_service, stop_service or expose_port.
prompts.why.lead: Port {port} won't open. Find the cause in the order below. Fix things only after I confirm.
prompts.why.leadFrom: Port {port} won't open from {from}. Find the cause in the order below. Fix things only after I confirm.
prompts.why.step5: 5. The connecting side: whether that device is online on the tailnet (list_devices), and whether it connected recently (who_uses(port: {port})).
prompts.why.step5From: 5. The connecting side: whether {from} is online on the tailnet (list_devices), and whether it connected recently (who_uses(port: {port})).
prompts.why.steps:
1. listening: list_ports(query: "{port}", include_system: true). If it isn't listed or listening=false, check its 🔔 state and last use with service_detail(port: {port}), and why it stopped with tail_logs(port: {port}).
2. bind scope: on loopback it won't open from outside this server. If canExpose=true, suggest expose_port to get a servedUrl; otherwise explain exposeBlocker or suggest binding to 0.0.0.0/tailnet.
3. served: if there's a servedUrl, check it's opened by that https URL and not confused with directUrl (http://…:port).
4. HTTP: http null means it isn't HTTP or doesn't answer; 4xx/5xx means an app problem → recent errors with tail_logs.
